title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes. There Grothendieck tests an axiomatic theory of combinatorial 'lieux' or figures, whose axioms are named Mog L1, Mog L2, etc. The test case is the simplest one: a 1-dimensional structure M built from a (partially) ordered set L.

The objects of M are of two kinds:
- 'points' P_x, for x in L;
- 'segments' S_{a,b}, for a<b, with open shadow Omb°(S_{a,b}) = ]a,b[.

Two relations appear. 'X || Y' (from the previous page) is comparability for points. 'X |o| Y' is a separation or 'foreignness' relation between figures (no common refinement).

The question is when M is 'fidèle' (faithful). Faithfulness is condition (*): if the open shadows of X and Y are disjoint, then X |o| Y. Grothendieck checks (*) case by case.

1. Two points. For X=P_x, Y=P_y, (*) says that distinct points are separated. For points, separation is comparability, so this forces L to be totally ordered. Conversely, this case of (*) is equivalent to total order.
2. A point and a segment. For X=P_x, Y=S_{a,b}, (*) reads: x ∉ ]a,b[ implies x ≤ a or x ≥ b. This is automatic in a total order.
3. Two segments. For X=S_{a,b}, Y=S_{a',b'}, one must show the contrapositive. Suppose neither b ≤ a' nor b' ≤ a holds, i.e. b > a' and b' > a. Then the segments have a common refinement, namely S_{max(a,a'), min(b,b')}. Grothendieck enumerates four cases by the relative positions of a, a' and of b, b':
   - a' ≤ a < b ≤ b': take S_{a,b};
   - a ≤ a' < b ≤ b': take S_{a',b};
   - a' ≤ a < b' ≤ b: take S_{a,b'};
   - a ≤ a' < b' ≤ b: take S_{a',b'}.

Conclusions:
- Lemma: M is faithful if and only if L is totally ordered.
- Corollary: M is 'parfait' if and only if L is totally ordered and divisible (dense). This combines with the previous page's lemma: Mog L2 holds iff L is divisible and condition (ii) holds, and (ii) is automatic for a total order.

The purpose is to calibrate the axioms of the new analysis situs on the 1-dimensional model, i.e. dense linear orders as 'tame' 1-dimensional spaces. This is the axis on which the line R is the model case.
errors: Minor gap: the open shadow of S_{a,b} is ]a,b[. If L is not divisible, the common refinement S_{max a, min b} can have an empty open interval. Then 'common refinement exists' does not literally mean 'open shadows meet'. The argument shows refinement exists; for the converse direction Grothendieck tacitly needs the shadows of the refinement to be nonempty, or else a combinatorial definition of Omb°. This is harmless for the lemma as stated, since the needed direction is the contrapositive, but the ambiguity is there.
The four-case enumeration silently uses b>a' and b'>a so that the chosen segments are nondegenerate. The cases are correct and exhaustive.

ideas.what: Faithfulness criterion for the combinatorial 1-dimensional 'lieu' attached to an ordered set: faithful iff L is totally ordered
ideas.modern_name: Linear orders as models of 1-dimensional tame/combinatorial spaces (cf. o-minimal 1-dimensional structure, interval combinatorics)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; o-minimality framework due to van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only announces a 'topologie modérée' program in general terms; this specific axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: 'Perfection' of M iff L is totally ordered and dense (divisible)
Common refinement of two overlapping intervals S_{max(a,a'),min(b,b')}
ideas.modern_name: Intersection of intervals in a linear order

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification of the axioms of Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 analysis situs on the trivial 1-dimensional model of an ordered set. The results are elementary order theory. It is of historical interest only as documentation of how he tested his axioms.
transcription_corrections: 'm.g.r.n' is uncertain; it is likely an abbreviation for the structure M under study, whose exact reading is unclear from the image.
In the segment case the image reads 'si on n'a pas b≤a' ou b'≤a, i.e. si on a b>a', b'>a' (both underlined).

In the corollary, the parenthetical '(et alors M est un ...)' ends with an illegible word, possibly an adjective like 'indivisible' or a similar term; 'divisible' at the start of the next line belongs to the condition on L.
